intro: Notion for museum curators on Mac is a powerful way to bridge the gap between heavy collection management systems and your daily research notes. You can use the Notion desktop app to track provenance, plan upcoming exhibitions, and organize donor communication in one place. By adding Lazur, you gain a voice assistant that helps you navigate your workspace, dictate complex notes, and find information without breaking your flow.
tldr: Use Notion as a flexible layer on top of your rigid collection management software.
Build databases for exhibition timelines, object research, and donor contacts.
Use ⌘ P to jump between your curatorial project pages instantly.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about specific data points on your screen.
Use ⌥ fn to dictate long-form research notes directly into your Notion pages.

blocks.text: Why curators need a flexible workspace on Mac

Your museum likely uses a dedicated collection management system like TMS or Axiell. These tools are excellent for long-term data storage but often feel rigid for daily planning. Notion works differently. It functions as a digital notebook where you can link research files, draft exhibition wall text, and track loan status. Keeping this on your Mac allows you to pull data from your browser or local files into your workspace with ease.

Exhibition planning involves hundreds of moving parts. A database in Notion helps you track each object, its loan status, and its current location. Create a board view to see the status of each item. Use properties to track insurance values, condition reports, and lender contact details. When you need to update a status, you can ask Lazur to point at the correct column if you get lost in a large table.
Speeding up research with voice dictation

Researching provenance or artist history often requires typing long notes. Using your Mac keyboard is fine, but dictation is faster. Hold the fn key on your keyboard and start speaking. Lazur will turn your voice into clean, formatted text right at your cursor. This is perfect for capturing thoughts while you look at high-resolution images of artifacts or read through digitized archives.
Practical tips for your Notion workspace

items: Use /template to create a standard format for new object research pages.
Add a Table of Contents to long exhibition planning documents to save scrolling.
Use the ⌘ Shift L shortcut to lock sensitive pages that contain donor information.
Create a linked database view to show only objects arriving in the next three months.
Use ⌘ P to search your entire workspace for specific artist names or accession numbers.

blocks.text: Curators often spend more time on grants and donor emails than on actual art. Use Notion to build a donor CRM. Link this to your research pages so you know which donors support which collections. If you are struggling to find a specific grant document, use the ⌘ P command. If the interface feels cluttered, ask Lazur to explain where the filter settings are located for your current database.

Do not try to replace your primary collection management system with Notion. Keep your official records in the system of record. Use Notion for the messy, creative work that happens before an object is fully cataloged. Also, avoid creating too many nested sub-pages. A flat structure with clear database properties is much easier to search using the built-in Mac tools.

Museum data is sensitive. Always check your workspace permissions. Ensure that only necessary staff have access to sensitive donor records or insurance information. Notion allows you to invite guests to specific pages. This is a great way to share a draft exhibition plan with a guest curator without giving them access to your entire database of collection records.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for museum inventory management?
faq.answer: Notion is great for tracking lists, but it is not a replacement for professional collection management systems like TMS or EMu. Use Notion for planning and research, and keep your official records in your museum software.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Notion desktop app?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac, including the Notion desktop app. You can hold the shortcut to ask questions about your screen or use dictation to write notes directly into your pages.

faq.question: How do I make my Notion workspace faster on Mac?
faq.answer: Use the desktop app instead of a web browser. Regularly clear your cache by pressing ⌘ R in the app. Keep your databases lean by using filters to hide old or inactive records.
